coreModelUse: Every finding gets a name and a reason, and the proof section insists on both sides before calling anything closed.

sections.why: Name the real task: audit your own router and close the openings nobody chose.
Activate the inventory, baseline and translation-versus-permission model the audit reuses.
Demonstrate the whole job on one example router: each finding walked to keep, close or unknown.
Show how each verdict was reached: own records first, then the authorized owner; unfamiliar stays unknown.
The apply sequence on the reader's own router, in order, one change at a time.
The reader records their own findings and verdicts; empty fields reset and are not evidence.
Integrate: inside view and outside attempt are separate proofs; one alone does not close the question.
Check the model: a failed outside attempt with a live LAN listener means the boundary is closed, not the service.
Consent and recovery: own router, owner's okay, and recorded changes can be re-added by name.
UPnP and home-router guidance grounds the audit.
Point at the lab boundary page the closed openings make safe to build.

rejected.why: The proof is two checks, not a packet path; the comparison carries it.
Router admin pages differ by vendor; invented commands would teach a UI nobody has.
